name: Camels
description: Bob likes to draw camels: with a single hump, two humps, three humps, etc. He draws a camel by connecting points on a coordinate plane. Now he's drawing camels with t humps, representing them as polylines in the plane. Each polyline consists of n vertices with coordinates ( x 1 , y 1 ) , ( x 2 , y 2 ) , ..., ( x n , y n ) . The first vertex has a coordinate x 1 = 1 , the second — x 2 = 2 , etc. Coordinates y i might be any, but should satisfy the following conditions: there should be t humps precisely, i.e. such indexes j ( 2 ≤ j ≤ n - 1 ), so that y j - 1 < y j > y j + 1 , there should be precisely t - 1 such indexes j ( 2 ≤ j ≤ n - 1 ), so that y j - 1 > y j < y j + 1 , no segment of a polyline should be parallel to the Ox -axis, all y i are integers between 1 and 4. For a series of his drawings of camels with t humps Bob wants to buy a notebook, but he doesn't know how many pages he will need. Output the amount of different polylines that can be drawn to represent camels with t humps for a given number n .
input_specification: The first line contains a pair of integers n and t ( 3 ≤ n ≤ 20 , 1 ≤ t ≤ 10 ).
output_specification: Output the required amount of camels with t humps.
approach_summary: Apply Knapsack and Basic Dynamic Programming paradigm under the Dynamic Programming (DP) framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
